intent.raw_query: Cambodia Angkor Wat + beaches, $1100, 10 days, November 2026

selected_hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Angkor Wat Temple Complex Sunrise Tour
experiences.description: Explore the world's largest religious monument at sunrise, wandering through the iconic towers and intricate bas-reliefs of Angkor Wat, then continue to the mysterious Bayon temple with its 216 serene stone faces and the jungle-engulfed Ta Prohm temple made famous by Tomb Raider.

experiences.name: Phnom Penh Historical Landmarks Tour
experiences.description: Visit the sobering Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum and the Killing Fields of Choeung Ek to understand Cambodia's tragic Khmer Rouge history, then contrast with the stunning Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda to appreciate the country's rich royal heritage and Buddhist culture.

experiences.name: Koh Rong Samloem Beach Escape
experiences.description: Take a ferry to the pristine Koh Rong Samloem island and spend the day on Saracen Bay or Lazy Beach, enjoying crystal-clear turquoise waters, white sand, and vibrant coral reefs perfect for snorkeling. Experience bioluminescent plankton glowing in the water after dark.

experiences.name: Cambodian Street Food and Market Tour
experiences.description: Dive into Cambodian culinary culture with a guided evening street food walk through the Old Market area, sampling local delicacies such as fish amok, lok lak beef, nom banh chok noodles, and adventurous fried insects. Visit the bustling Psar Chas market and learn about Khmer spices and cooking traditions.
experiences.location: Old Market (Psar Chas) District, Siem Reap

experiences.name: Kampot River and Pepper Plantation Cultural Tour
experiences.description: Explore the charming French colonial town of Kampot by tuk-tuk, then take a boat ride along the Kampot River through mangroves and fishing villages. Visit a world-renowned Kampot pepper plantation to learn about the cultivation of Cambodia's prized export, and explore nearby Bokor Hill Station ruins for panoramic views and colonial history.
experiences.location: Kampot Town and Surroundings, Kampot Province

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Cambodia
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and take a tuk-tuk to your boutique stay near Angkor Archaeological Park (approx $5–7 USD). Check in, freshen up, and take a slow walk around the immediate neighborhood to get oriented. Visit the nearby Angkor Night Market area for a gentle first look at local life.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Pub Street and the Old Market (Phsar Chas) area in Siem Reap town center (~10 min tuk-tuk ride). Browse local handicraft stalls, pick up a SIM card if needed, and soak in the lively atmosphere. Watch a free traditional Apsara dance performance preview outside some restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight)
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or a local noodle stall near the hotel (~$2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Khmer Kitchen Restaurant on Pub Street — try Amok fish curry and jasmine rice (~$4–6 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Exchange a small amount of USD or use ATMs at the airport. Cambodia widely accepts USD. Negotiate tuk-tuk fares in advance. A local SIM card (Smart or Cellcard) costs ~$2–3 and provides good data coverage.

day_by_day.morning: Rise before dawn (4:30 AM) for the iconic Angkor Wat sunrise. Hire a tuk-tuk driver for the day (~$15–18 USD). Watch the sun rise over the temple's reflection pool — one of Southeast Asia's most breathtaking sights. Spend the morning exploring Angkor Wat's galleries, bas-reliefs depicting the Churning of the Ocean of Milk, and the central towers. Buy a 3-day Angkor Pass (~$62 USD) at the ticket office the evening before or early morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or tuk-tuk to Angkor Thom complex (~2 km north). Explore the South Gate with its massive stone faces, the awe-inspiring Bayon Temple with 216 serene stone faces, the Baphuon temple-mountain, and the Elephant Terrace. Take time at the Terrace of the Leper King.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap town. Visit the Angkor Night Market for budget souvenir shopping. Enjoy a traditional Khmer massage on Sivatha Street (~$7–9 USD for one hour).

meals.breakfast: Early snack from a street vendor near Angkor Wat — sticky rice or baguette with egg (~$1–2 USD)
meals.lunch: Local restaurant near Angkor Thom — rice with grilled pork or lok lak (~$3–4 USD)
meals.dinner: Marum Restaurant (social enterprise training restaurant) — excellent Khmer dishes (~$5–8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Wear light, breathable clothing and bring a hat and sunscreen. Shoulders and knees must be covered inside temples. Carry at least 1.5L of water. November weather should be pleasant — dry season beginning, around 28–32°C.

day_by_day.morning: Use your 3-day Angkor Pass. Head to Ta Prohm temple — famously left partially unrestored with giant silk-cotton and strangler fig trees growing through the ruins (made famous by Tomb Raider). Arrive early (~7:00 AM) before tour groups arrive. Explore the atmospheric moss-covered corridors and root-entwined doorways.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Banteay Kdei, a Buddhist monastery temple, followed by a peaceful walk around Sra Srang — a royal bathing reservoir with beautiful lakeside views. Continue to Pre Rup, a 10th-century temple-mountain with panoramic views, ideal for late afternoon light photography.
day_by_day.evening: Back in Siem Reap, explore the Artisans Angkor workshop (free entry) to see local craftspeople creating silk, lacquerware, and stone carvings. Browse their shop for high-quality ethical souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Bai Sach Chrouk (pork and rice) from a local morning market stall near your hotel (~$1.50 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside noodle soup (Kuy Teav) near Ta Prohm (~$2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Genevieve's Restaurant near Old Market — try Khmer red curry with coconut milk (~$4–6 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Ta Prohm gets very crowded by 9 AM — early arrival is essential. Hire your same tuk-tuk driver from Day 2 for a better rate. Carry cash as there are no ATMs inside the park.

day_by_day.morning: Final day on the 3-day Angkor Pass. Venture to the outlying temples — hire a tuk-tuk for the 'Grand Circuit.' Start with Preah Khan, a vast jungle temple dedicated to the father of Jayavarman VII, with beautiful tree-root-entwined walls and long atmospheric corridors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Neak Pean, a unique island temple set in a large reservoir (accessible via boardwalk), then Ta Som with its iconic tree-covered eastern gopura gateway. Finish at East Mebon, a 10th-century temple built on an artificial island.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Apsara Dance performance at Smile of Angkor or Cambodian Cultural Village — a cultural highlight showing classical Khmer dance rooted in Angkor-era court traditions (~$12–15 USD including dinner buffet, or ~$8 USD show only).

meals.breakfast: Nom Banh Chok (Khmer noodles with green fish curry sauce) from a local market (~$1.50 USD)
meals.lunch: Roadside BBQ near Preah Khan — grilled meats and sticky rice (~$3 USD)
meals.dinner: Apsara dance dinner buffet or local Khmer BBQ restaurant (~$5–8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: This completes your 3-day Angkor Pass. Keep your ticket safe as guards check it at every temple. Consider tipping your tuk-tuk driver if they've been reliable — $1–2 extra is appreciated.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Banteay Srei — the 'Citadel of Women,' located 25 km north of Siem Reap. This 10th-century temple is renowned for its extraordinarily intricate pink sandstone carvings, considered the finest in all of Angkor. Hire a tuk-tuk or rent a bicycle for the journey (~$12–15 USD tuk-tuk return). Combine with a visit to the nearby Landmine Museum — a sobering and important exhibit about Cambodia's tragic history with landmines.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Siem Reap and visit the Cambodian Cultural Village — an open-air museum showcasing traditional Khmer village life, ethnic minority cultures, and historical dioramas (~$5 USD entry). A good budget-friendly cultural immersion experience.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Siem Reap's vibrant street food scene around the Night Market and riverside. Try local snacks like fried insects (adventurous!), fresh spring rolls, and sugarcane juice.

meals.breakfast: French baguette with pâté from a local bakery — a Cambodian-French colonial legacy (~$1.50 USD)
meals.lunch: Restaurant near Banteay Srei — set Khmer lunch menu (~$3–5 USD)
meals.dinner: Street food dinner at Night Market — budget $3–5 USD for a full spread of local snacks and dishes

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei requires a separate entry fee (~$3 USD, not included in Angkor Pass). The Landmine Museum entry is by donation. Wear sunscreen for the outdoor Cultural Village visit.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take a morning bus from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh (approx 5–6 hours, ~$6–8 USD with Giant Ibis, Mekong Express, or Larryta bus companies). Book tickets the day before. Depart around 7:00–8:00 AM. Enjoy the countryside scenery along National Road 6.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh around 1:00–2:00 PM. Check into a budget guesthouse near the riverfront (dorms from $5 USD, private rooms from $12–15 USD — recommended: Mad Monkey Hostel or Onederz Hostel). After settling in, visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda (~$10 USD entry) — Cambodia's most iconic royal landmark with stunning Khmer architecture and a pagoda floor made of 5,000 silver tiles.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Sisowath Quay riverside promenade as the sun sets over the Tonle Sap and Mekong rivers. Browse the riverside night market. Enjoy the cool evening breeze.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at your Siem Reap hotel or a nearby café before departure (~$2–3 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed snacks on the bus or stop at a roadside restaurant during the journey (~$2–4 USD)
meals.dinner: Rooftop restaurant near the riverfront — try Fish Amok or Lok Lak (~$4–6 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Book bus tickets in advance, especially on weekends. Giant Ibis is the most reliable and comfortable budget option. Store valuables securely on the bus. Phnom Penh is more spread out than Siem Reap — tuk-tuks and PassApp (local ride-hailing app) are the best ways to get around.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a former high school turned Khmer Rouge prison, now a deeply moving memorial to the victims of the genocide (~$5 USD entry, audio guide $3 USD). This is essential for understanding Cambodia's modern history. Allow 2–3 hours for a respectful and thorough visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a tuk-tuk to the Choeung Ek Killing Fields Memorial (~15 km from city center, ~$5 USD tuk-tuk). The memorial and audio tour (~$6 USD) provide profound insight into the atrocities of the Khmer Rouge regime (1975–1979). Return to the city and visit the National Museum of Cambodia (~$10 USD) — housing the world's finest collection of Khmer art and sculpture.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Central Market (Phsar Thmei) — a stunning Art Deco yellow dome building from 1937. Browse local goods and pick up affordable souvenirs. Enjoy dinner near the riverside.

meals.breakfast: Bánh mì-style Cambodian sandwich from a street cart near your hostel (~$1.50 USD)
meals.lunch: Local restaurant near Tuol Sleng — rice and stir-fry (~$3–4 USD)
meals.dinner: Friends Restaurant (social enterprise) — excellent tapas-style Khmer food (~$5–8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek are emotionally intense — allow yourself time to process. Photography is permitted but be respectful. Dress modestly. Combine both sites in one half-day with a tuk-tuk driver (~$10–12 USD for both stops).

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take a morning bus or shared taxi from Phnom Penh to Sihanoukville (approx 4 hours, ~$5–8 USD). Depart around 7:00–8:00 AM. Sihanoukville is Cambodia's main beach hub on the Gulf of Thailand. Check into a budget guesthouse on Otres Beach (~$10–18 USD/night for private room — Otres is quieter and more backpacker-friendly than the main town).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Otres Beach and spend the afternoon relaxing on the quiet, palm-fringed shoreline. The water is warm and calm in November (dry season beginning). Rent a beach chair (~$1–2 USD) and swim in the turquoise Gulf of Thailand waters. Explore the beach on foot.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a beachfront bar on Otres Beach. Watch the brilliant sunset over the Gulf of Thailand. Enjoy fresh seafood at a beachfront restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the Phnom Penh bus station or hostel (~$2 USD)
meals.lunch: Roadside food during bus journey or upon arrival (~$2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Fresh grilled seafood BBQ on Otres Beach — whole grilled fish, prawns, rice (~$6–10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Sihanoukville's main town has changed significantly due to development — Otres Beach (Otres 1 and Otres 2) is recommended for a more relaxed, budget-friendly beach experience. November is the start of the dry season — expect mostly sunny skies with possible brief showers.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning boat to Koh Rong Sanloem island (~45 min, ~$15–20 USD return) — one of Cambodia's most beautiful islands with crystal-clear water and white sand beaches. Head to Saracen Bay or the quieter M'Pai Bay. Snorkel in the coral reefs (snorkel rental ~$3–5 USD). The water visibility in November is typically excellent.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the island — hike through the jungle to a hidden beach, or simply relax and swim. Try kayaking around the bay (~$5–8 USD/hour rental). If staying overnight isn't in the budget, catch the late afternoon boat back to Sihanoukville.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Otres Beach by late afternoon. Watch the sunset from the beach. Explore the Otres Village area for local restaurants and a relaxed evening atmosphere. Try a fresh coconut (~$1 USD) while watching the stars — light pollution is minimal here.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast — eggs, toast, fruit (~$2–3 USD)
meals.lunch: Beachside restaurant on Koh Rong Sanloem — fresh fish sandwich or coconut curry (~$4–6 USD)
meals.dinner: Otres Beach restaurant — Khmer fish soup or grilled squid with vegetables and rice (~$4–7 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Boats to Koh Rong Sanloem depart from Sihanoukville Port — book tickets the evening before at the port or through your guesthouse. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a dry bag for valuables, and cash as ATMs are limited on the island. Bioluminescent plankton can sometimes be seen at night in the bay — ask locals for the best spots.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on Otres Beach — enjoy a slow breakfast and a last swim in the Gulf of Thailand. Take a walk along the full length of Otres Beach to soak in the scenery. Do some last-minute souvenir shopping at beachside stalls — sarongs, shell jewelry, and handmade crafts are affordable and locally made.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return bus or shared taxi from Sihanoukville to Phnom Penh (~4 hours, ~$5–8 USD) or Siem Reap depending on your departure flight. If flying out of Phnom Penh, depart Sihanoukville by noon. Use the journey time to reflect on the trip and organize photos. If time allows before your departure, visit Phnom Penh's riverfront one last time for a final Khmer coffee.
day_by_day.evening: Departure preparations — head to Phnom Penh International Airport or your onward destination. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your international flight for check-in and security.

meals.breakfast: Final Cambodian breakfast on the beach — fruit smoothie bowl or Khmer porridge (Bobor) (~$2–3 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed snacks or roadside stop during the return bus journey (~$2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Airport meal or a quick stop at a local restaurant near Phnom Penh airport (~$4–6 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Final budget summary estimate for 10 days: Accommodation ~$80–120 USD, Transport ~$50–70 USD, Food ~$60–80 USD, Entrance fees ~$90–100 USD, Activities ~$30–50 USD — Total approximately $310–420 USD excluding international flights. Keep small USD bills handy for tips and small purchases throughout Cambodia. Departure tax is typically included in international flight tickets.

trip_options.title: Classic Cambodia Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your boutique stay near Angkor Archaeological Park. After freshening up, take a gentle orientation stroll through the nearby temple grounds — visit the South Gate of Angkor Thom and the Bayon Temple for a soft introduction to the ancient city. The late afternoon light makes the stone faces glow beautifully.
day_by_day.evening: Head into Siem Reap town to explore the vibrant Pub Street area and the Old Market (Psar Chas). Browse local handicrafts and soak up the lively atmosphere as the city comes alive after dark.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or light snack at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or a café near your hotel upon arrival — try a bowl of Khmer noodle soup (kuy teav) for around $3–5
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cuisine Wat Damnak or Mahob Restaurant in Siem Reap town — enjoy authentic Khmer tasting menus featuring amok, lok lak, and fresh spring rolls ($15–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Confirm hotel transfer in advance. November is the start of the dry season in Cambodia, expect warm temperatures around 28–32°C with low humidity — ideal temple-visiting weather.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early (5:00 AM) for the iconic Angkor Wat sunrise — one of the most breathtaking experiences in Southeast Asia. Watch the temple's five towers reflect in the long rectangular pond as the sky turns pink and gold. Explore the outer galleries of Angkor Wat, including the famous bas-reliefs depicting Hindu epics and the Churning of the Ocean of Milk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Angkor Wat's inner sanctuaries and climb to the upper terrace for panoramic views. After lunch, visit the nearby Angkor Thom complex including the Bayon Temple (with its 216 serene stone faces), the Baphuon, and the Terrace of the Elephants.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your hotel for a rest, then enjoy dinner near the hotel or in Siem Reap town. Consider attending an Apsara dance performance — a traditional Khmer classical dance recognized by UNESCO.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at your hotel or packed snacks before sunrise — most boutique hotels offer early breakfast for temple visitors
meals.lunch: Local restaurant near Angkor complex — try a set Khmer lunch with fish amok, rice, and fresh coconut water ($6–10)
meals.dinner: Dinner and Apsara show at Angkor Village Theatre or Smile of Angkor ($20–35 per person including show)

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a 3-day Angkor Pass ($62 USD) — it offers the best value for multiple days of temple exploration. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and plenty of water. Modest dress required (shoulders and knees covered).

day_by_day.morning: Explore the jungle-wrapped temple of Ta Prohm — famously known as the 'Tomb Raider temple' — where massive silk-cotton tree roots dramatically engulf ancient stone walls. Arrive early to beat the crowds. Nearby, visit Banteay Kdei, a quieter Buddhist monastery temple.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Pre Rup temple for sweeping views from its pyramid-like summit, then head to the East Mebon temple, built on an artificial island. Stop by the Angkor National Museum in Siem Reap for cultural context — beautifully curated exhibits on Khmer civilization, art, and religion ($12 entry).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the artisan village of Artisans Angkor at their Siem Reap workshop — watch craftspeople carve stone, lacquer wood, and weave silk using traditional techniques. Browse their fair-trade shop for authentic souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel — enjoy tropical fruits, baguette with jam (French colonial influence), and Khmer coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch from a local market stall near the temple complex — fresh baguette sandwiches, grilled corn, and fresh fruit ($3–5)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Haven Restaurant — a social enterprise training at-risk youth in hospitality. Excellent Western-Khmer fusion in a lovely garden setting ($12–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Ta Prohm gets crowded mid-morning. Go at opening (7:30 AM) for the best experience. Your 3-day Angkor Pass covers all sites today.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Banteay Srei — a stunning 10th-century temple dedicated to Shiva, located about 25 km from Siem Reap. Known as the 'Citadel of Women,' it features the most intricate and detailed pink sandstone carvings in all of Angkor. Combine with a visit to the Kbal Spean 'River of a Thousand Lingas' — a 1.5-hour jungle hike to a riverbed carved with thousands of Hindu symbols.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Siem Reap and visit the Landmine Museum — a sobering but essential cultural experience documenting Cambodia's tragic history with landmines and the ongoing demining efforts ($5 entry, supports a vital cause). Afterward, relax at a café in town.
day_by_day.evening: Take a traditional Khmer cooking class in the evening — learn to prepare dishes like fish amok in banana leaf, green mango salad, and banana blossom soup. A hands-on cultural experience you'll carry home.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel before the early departure to Banteay Srei
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant in the Banteay Srei area or pack a light lunch from town ($5–8)
meals.dinner: Enjoy the dishes you cook in your cooking class! Most classes include a full dinner of your prepared meal ($25–35 per person including class)

day_by_day.notes: Hire a tuk-tuk driver for the day for the Banteay Srei trip — negotiate a full-day rate of $20–25. The Kbal Spean hike involves a moderate uphill trail — wear sturdy shoes and bring water.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take a morning bus or private van from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh (approximately 5–6 hours, $10–15 by bus or $60–80 private transfer). Enjoy the Cambodian countryside scenery along the way — rice paddies, stilted wooden houses, and Buddhist pagodas dot the landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh. Check in to your mid-range hotel in the riverside area. Visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda — Cambodia's most impressive royal complex featuring glittering temple spires, sacred Buddha statues, and manicured gardens ($10 entry).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Sisowath Quay riverside promenade as the sun sets over the Tonle Sap and Mekong rivers. Explore the Foreign Correspondents' Club (FCC) for sundowner drinks with a colonial-era atmosphere and river views.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Siem Reap hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch stop en route — roadside Cambodian restaurant serving rice dishes and fresh soups ($4–7)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Malis Restaurant in Phnom Penh — upscale Khmer cuisine in an elegant garden setting, celebrating traditional recipes ($15–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book your Phnom Penh accommodation in the riverside/BKK1 area for easy access to key sights. The Giant Ibis or Mekong Express buses are reliable and comfortable options for the Siem Reap–Phnom Penh route.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a former high school converted into a brutal detention center during the Khmer Rouge regime (1975–1979). This deeply moving and historically essential site offers a profound understanding of Cambodia's 20th-century tragedy ($3 entry, audio guides available).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Choeung Ek Genocidal Center (Killing Fields) — located 15 km from the city center. The memorial stupa containing thousands of skulls and the peaceful grounds serve as a testament to resilience and remembrance ($6 entry with excellent audio guide). Return to the city and visit the National Museum of Cambodia — housing the world's finest collection of Khmer sculpture and artifacts ($5 entry).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Bassac Lane bar and restaurant strip for dinner and evening drinks. Browse the Russian Market (Psar Toul Tom Poung) if it's still open in the late afternoon for local crafts, clothing, and street food.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel — Phnom Penh is famous for its French-influenced café culture; enjoy a café au lait and a croissant
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local Khmer restaurant near the National Museum — try bai sach chrouk (pork and rice) or num banh chok (Khmer noodles) ($4–7)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Romdeng Restaurant — a social enterprise serving traditional Cambodian cuisine including deep-fried tarantulas for the adventurous! Beautiful colonial villa setting ($12–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek visits are emotionally heavy — allow time for reflection. These sites are crucial for understanding Cambodia's history and culture. Dress respectfully. Hiring a tuk-tuk for the full day in Phnom Penh costs around $15–20.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take an early morning bus or minivan from Phnom Penh to Kampot (approximately 3 hours, $8–12) or directly to Sihanoukville/Otres Beach (4 hours, $10–15). Kampot is highly recommended — a charming riverside colonial town near the coast, ideal for a balanced cultural-beach experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Kampot. Check in to your guesthouse or boutique hotel. Explore the compact French colonial old town on foot — admire the faded pastel architecture, riverside promenade, and quirky cafés. Rent a bicycle ($2–3/day) to explore at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset boat cruise on the Kampot River — a magical experience as fireflies begin to light up the mangroves after dark. Many guesthouses and tour operators offer these for $8–12 per person.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Phnom Penh hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch on arrival in Kampot — try the local specialty Kampot pepper crab or a pepper-infused beef lok lak at a riverside restaurant ($8–15)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Rikitikitavi or Epic Arts Café in Kampot — riverside dining with fresh Khmer and international options ($10–18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Kampot is renowned for its world-famous Kampot pepper — one of the finest peppers in the world. November is perfect beach and coastal weather in southern Cambodia — warm, sunny, and dry.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Bokor National Park — a dramatic plateau rising 1,080 meters above sea level with sweeping views of the Gulf of Thailand. Visit the haunting abandoned French hill station including the old casino-hotel, church ruins, and waterfall. Rent a motorbike or join a guided tour ($15–25).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Kampot and head to Kep — a tiny beach town 25 km away, famous for its crab market and tranquil seafront. Visit the Kep Crab Market and watch fishermen bring in fresh catches. Relax on Kep Beach or take a short boat ride to Rabbit Island (Koh Tonsay) for crystal-clear water and white sand.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kampot for dinner. Explore the town's laid-back bar scene along the riverside — perfect for a relaxed evening with cold Angkor beer and live music.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your guesthouse in Kampot — fresh fruit, eggs, and Khmer coffee
meals.lunch: Fresh crab lunch at Kep Crab Market — steamed or stir-fried crab with Kampot pepper is a must-have ($10–18)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Baraca or The Rusty Keyhole in Kampot — excellent riverside atmosphere with wood-fired pizza, fresh seafood, and Khmer dishes ($10–15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The road to Bokor can be steep and winding — a motorbike requires confidence. Alternatively, hire a tuk-tuk or join a group tour. Rabbit Island day trips cost around $5–8 return by boat from Kep pier.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Otres Beach near Sihanoukville (approximately 1.5 hours from Kampot, $8–12 by shared minivan). Otres Beach — specifically Otres 2 — remains one of Cambodia's most beautiful and laid-back stretches of coastline, with calm turquoise water and a relaxed atmosphere. Check in to a beachfront bungalow or guesthouse.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon on the beach — swim in the warm Gulf of Thailand waters, lounge under a palm tree, or rent a kayak to paddle along the coast. Book a snorkeling trip to nearby islands like Koh Rong Sanloem or Koh Ta Kiev (half-day trips from $15–25 per person).
day_by_day.evening: Beach bonfire and barbecue dinner at one of the beachfront restaurants. Watch the stars over the Gulf of Thailand — November skies in southern Cambodia are exceptionally clear.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Kampot guesthouse before departure
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Otres Beach — fresh seafood grilled on charcoal, green papaya salad, and fresh coconut ($8–12)
meals.dinner: Beachfront barbecue dinner at your guesthouse or a nearby beach shack — grilled prawns, squid, and fish with rice and cold beers ($12–18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Sihanoukville city itself has changed significantly in recent years — stick to Otres Beach (Otres 1 or 2) which retains its charm and is much quieter. Confirm your return transport to Phnom Penh for Day 10.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on Otres Beach — enjoy a slow breakfast, a last swim, and a peaceful walk along the shoreline. Pack up and check out. Take a morning minivan back to Phnom Penh (4 hours, $10–15) or directly to Phnom Penh International Airport depending on your departure flight time.
day_by_day.afternoon: If time permits before your flight, stop at a final café in Phnom Penh for Khmer iced coffee and pick up last-minute souvenirs — Kampot pepper, silk scarves, or hand-carved wooden items from a reputable fair-trade shop like Daughters of Cambodia or Watthan Artisans.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Phnom Penh International Airport. Reflect on 10 extraordinary days of ancient temples, living culture, colonial history, and tropical beaches across the Kingdom of Wonder.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at your Otres Beach guesthouse — enjoy tropical fruits and a fresh smoothie bowl
meals.lunch: Quick lunch in Phnom Penh near the airport or at a riverside café — a farewell bowl of kuy teav noodle soup ($4–6)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your international flight for check-in at Phnom Penh International Airport. If flying from Siem Reap instead, book an internal flight (Phnom Penh–Siem Reap, ~$60–90) or plan your itinerary in reverse. Keep $25 USD cash for the Cambodia departure tax if not included in your ticket.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Cambodia Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged to boutique hotel in Angkor Archaeological Park area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to hotel, check-in, and settle into your suite. Enjoy a welcome drink and orientation with your personal concierge. Take a leisurely stroll through the hotel gardens to acclimatize to the Cambodian warmth and humidity.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the hotel's rooftop or poolside terrace overlooking the lush surroundings. Gentle introduction to Cambodian culture with a private Apsara dance performance arranged at the hotel.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight
meals.lunch: Light welcome spread at the hotel upon arrival — fresh tropical fruits, Cambodian spring rolls, and chilled coconut water prepared by the hotel chef
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cuisine Wat Damnak, one of Siem Reap's finest restaurants offering modern Cambodian tasting menus with seasonal local ingredients and wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Request early check-in in advance. Ensure private airport transfer is pre-booked with a chilled towel and welcome refreshments in the vehicle. November in Cambodia is cool and dry — ideal travel weather.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn private guided tour of Angkor Wat to witness the legendary sunrise over the temple spires reflected in the lotus ponds. Accompanied by a senior archaeologist-guide for deep historical and spiritual context. Explore the bas-reliefs and inner sanctum before the crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploration of the Angkor complex with a visit to Angkor Thom — the Bayon Temple with its 216 serene stone faces, the Elephant Terrace, and the Terrace of the Leper King. Enjoy a private air-conditioned tuk-tuk or vintage Jeep transfer between sites.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a rejuvenating spa treatment — traditional Khmer massage and herbal compress therapy at the hotel's luxury spa. Freshen up for a refined dinner in town.

meals.breakfast: Pre-sunrise light breakfast box prepared by the hotel — croissants, fresh fruit, thermos of Cambodian coffee, and energy bars for the early temple visit
meals.lunch: Private picnic lunch arranged within the Angkor complex at a scenic shaded pavilion — chilled rice paper rolls, grilled chicken skewers, tropical fruit, and iced jasmine tea
meals.dinner: Dinner at Malis Restaurant, celebrated for its refined Cambodian royal cuisine in an elegant open-air setting — try the amok fish and lotus stem salad

day_by_day.notes: Wear light, breathable clothing and comfortable walking shoes. Bring sunscreen and a hat. Angkor Wat requires covered shoulders and knees — a sarong can be purchased at the gate.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to Ta Prohm — the iconic jungle temple famously featured in Tomb Raider, with ancient silk-cotton trees dramatically enveloping the stone ruins. Your expert guide will narrate the Khmer Empire's history and the temple's restoration story.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the lesser-visited but spectacular Preah Khan temple — a vast monastic complex with long corridors, intricate carvings, and a serene atmosphere far from the main tourist crowds. Followed by a visit to the Neak Pean island temple and its symbolic pools.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private sunset helicopter flight over the Angkor Archaeological Park for a breathtaking aerial perspective of the entire ancient city complex. Return for a candlelit dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full à la carte breakfast at the hotel — eggs Benedict with Cambodian herbs, fresh baguette, tropical fruit platter, and freshly brewed Cambodian Mondulkiri coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Viroth's Restaurant — a sophisticated Siem Reap institution serving refined Khmer dishes in a beautiful colonial-style villa setting
meals.dinner: Private in-room or poolside candlelit dinner curated by the hotel's executive chef — a bespoke multi-course Cambodian-French fusion menu with champagne

day_by_day.notes: Book the helicopter sunset flight well in advance as slots are limited. The flight typically lasts 30–45 minutes and offers unparalleled views of Angkor Wat, Angkor Thom, and the surrounding jungle.

day_by_day.morning: Private cultural immersion experience — visit a traditional Cambodian village near Siem Reap for a hands-on silk weaving workshop at a local artisan cooperative. Learn about the revival of Cambodia's ancient silk traditions nearly lost during the Khmer Rouge era.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Artisans Angkor workshop and boutique — a social enterprise preserving traditional Khmer crafts including lacquerware, stone carving, and silversmithing. Followed by a curated visit to the Angkor National Museum for a comprehensive historical overview of the Khmer Empire.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the hotel followed by a private cooking class with a master Khmer chef — learn to prepare three signature Cambodian dishes including fish amok, lok lak, and mango sticky rice.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — Cambodian-style congee with ginger and crispy shallots, fresh papaya, and Cambodian iced coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Sugar Palm Restaurant — a beloved Siem Reap spot serving authentic family-recipe Khmer cuisine in a charming wooden house setting
meals.dinner: Enjoy the dishes you prepared in your cooking class served as a private dinner at the hotel, paired with selected Cambodian craft beers and local fruit wines

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class is a highly immersive and memorable experience — request a vegetarian or dietary-specific menu variation if needed. The Artisans Angkor boutique is an excellent place for high-quality, ethically sourced souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning private boat excursion on the Tonlé Sap Lake — Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lake. Explore the extraordinary floating villages of Kompong Phluk, where entire communities live on stilted houses above the water. Guided by a local expert with deep knowledge of the lake's ecology and culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue on the lake to observe the flooded forest — a magical landscape of submerged trees and wildlife unique to the Tonlé Sap ecosystem. Return to Siem Reap for an afternoon at leisure at the hotel pool and spa.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant Siem Reap Old Market (Psar Chas) area on a private guided evening food tour — sample street delicacies including Khmer crepes, grilled corn, and fresh sugarcane juice, then browse boutique galleries on Kandal Village's art street.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel before departure — fresh fruit, yogurt, granola, and Cambodian coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch aboard the private boat on Tonlé Sap — a specially prepared picnic of fresh lake fish, sticky rice, and seasonal vegetables with cold pressed juices
meals.dinner: Dinner at Embassy Restaurant & Lounge — a chic rooftop dining experience with panoramic views of Siem Reap, serving contemporary Cambodian cuisine with international influences

day_by_day.notes: Water levels on Tonlé Sap vary by season — in November the lake begins to recede, revealing the stilted villages in their full dramatic height. Bring insect repellent for the evening food tour.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer to Siem Reap airport for a short domestic flight to Sihanoukville, then onward transfer to Koh Rong Sanloem or Song Saa Private Island — Cambodia's premier luxury beach destination. Check in to an overwater villa or beachfront suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: Settle into your island villa and spend the afternoon at leisure on the pristine white sand beach. Enjoy complimentary non-motorized water sports — kayaking, paddleboarding, and snorkeling in the crystal-clear turquoise Gulf of Thailand waters.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on your private villa deck or at the overwater bar. Enjoy a welcome seafood dinner at the island's signature restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel in Siem Reap before departure — continental spread with pastries, cold cuts, and fresh juices
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the island resort upon arrival — fresh seafood platter, tropical salads, and chilled coconut water
meals.dinner: Dinner at the island's fine dining restaurant — freshly caught seafood including grilled lobster, tiger prawns, and whole fish with Cambodian herbs, paired with premium white wines

day_by_day.notes: Song Saa Private Island and Koh Rong Sanloem's Lazy Beach area offer the most luxurious options on Cambodia's islands. Book island accommodation well in advance as inventory is very limited. The flight from Siem Reap to Sihanoukville takes approximately 45 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided snorkeling or scuba diving excursion to the coral reefs surrounding the island — explore vibrant marine life including reef fish, sea turtles, and coral gardens. Certified PADI dive instructors available for beginners.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private catamaran sailing trip around the archipelago — visit secluded beaches and hidden lagoons accessible only by boat. Anchor for a swim stop in a pristine bay with a floating lunch served on deck.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the island for a luxury spa treatment — a couples' massage in an open-air jungle spa pavilion using local ingredients such as lemongrass, kaffir lime, and coconut oil.

meals.breakfast: In-villa breakfast served on your private deck — eggs cooked to order, smoked salmon, tropical fruit, freshly baked pastries, and premium Cambodian coffee
meals.lunch: Floating seafood BBQ lunch on the catamaran — grilled fish, squid, and vegetables with rice and fresh lime dipping sauces, served with chilled Cambodian beer and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Private beachside dinner under the stars — a bespoke tasting menu designed by the island chef, featuring Cambodian coastal flavors with a French technique, paired with a curated wine selection

day_by_day.notes: November is an excellent time for island activities — the sea is calm and visibility for snorkeling and diving is exceptional. Bring reef-safe sunscreen to protect the coral ecosystems.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga session on the beach led by a private instructor, followed by a guided kayaking tour through mangrove forests and sea caves along the island's coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisure afternoon on the beach — enjoy the resort's infinity pool, hammocks, and beach club amenities. Optional: arrange a private fishing trip with local fishermen and have your catch prepared for dinner.
day_by_day.evening: Bonfire and stargazing session on a secluded beach arranged by the resort — with a private butler, a bottle of champagne, and a telescope for constellation viewing in Cambodia's clear November skies.

meals.breakfast: Healthy breakfast bowl at the resort beach café — açaí bowl, fresh tropical fruits, granola, and cold-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Casual beach club lunch — grilled fish tacos, fresh spring rolls, and coconut sorbet
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort — if you went fishing, your catch prepared as a whole roasted fish with Cambodian spices; otherwise a seafood tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The bonfire stargazing experience should be booked through the resort concierge in advance. Cambodia's islands have minimal light pollution, making for spectacular night sky viewing.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure on the island — final swim, beach walk, or spa treatment. Late morning transfer back to Sihanoukville by speedboat, then onward to Phnom Penh by private charter flight or luxury vehicle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to a luxury hotel in Phnom Penh (recommended: Raffles Hotel Le Royal, a legendary colonial-era property). Afternoon guided visit to the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda — Cambodia's most magnificent royal complex with its gleaming spires and sacred Buddha statues.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise along the Mekong and Tonlé Sap rivers on a private luxury boat — witness the confluence of the two great rivers at dusk with cocktails and canapés served on deck.

meals.breakfast: Final island breakfast on your villa deck — a full spread of fresh fruits, pastries, eggs, and Cambodian iced coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Topaz Restaurant in Phnom Penh — a refined French-Cambodian restaurant beloved by diplomats and discerning travelers, set in a beautiful colonial villa
meals.dinner: Dinner at Khéma La Poste, Phnom Penh's most prestigious restaurant located in a restored 1900s French post office building — exceptional French-Cambodian cuisine with an extensive wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: The Royal Palace requires covered shoulders and knees. The private Mekong sunset cruise can be arranged through the Raffles concierge and typically lasts 90 minutes to 2 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Poignant and important guided visit to the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) and the Choeung Ek Killing Fields Memorial — a deeply moving and essential cultural and historical experience to understand Cambodia's 20th-century history. Accompanied by a sensitive, expert historian guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Cambodia — a stunning terracotta building housing the world's finest collection of Khmer art and sculpture. Followed by a walk through the charming French Quarter and riverside promenade. Final luxury shopping at boutiques along Street 240 for Cambodian silk, jewelry, and artisan crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a top Phnom Penh restaurant, followed by a final evening stroll along the Phnom Penh riverside. Private luxury transfer to Phnom Penh International Airport for your departure flight.

meals.breakfast: Lavish full breakfast at Raffles Hotel Le Royal — the legendary 'Femme Fatale' buffet or à la carte in the elegant Café Monivong
meals.lunch: Lunch at Romdeng Restaurant — a celebrated social enterprise restaurant serving traditional Cambodian countryside cuisine in a beautiful French villa, staffed by at-risk youth
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Malis Phnom Penh — the capital branch of Cambodia's most acclaimed fine dining restaurant, featuring the full spectrum of royal Khmer cuisine with premium wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek visits are emotionally intense — allow time for reflection. An expert guide is essential to provide context and navigate the experience respectfully. Confirm departure flight time and arrange airport transfer with the hotel concierge at least 3 hours before departure.
